files.finding: The released fine-tuning script selects NAG, clipping0.1, update-freq6, sequence-level train rate0.5, rep_reduce_gamma0.5 and reset optimizer/scheduler. It loads a validation-selected checkpoint.
Each task train_step chooses pseudo loss with probability0.5, falling back to CE on invalid pseudo construction. The task calls backward but not optimizer.step.
Trainer clears gradients before looping over grouped samples, calls task backward per sample, normalizes by sample size, clips once, and steps once after the group.
update_freq groups minibatches with GroupedIterator and passes each group to trainer.train_step.

inference: The released update-freq6 fine-tuning recipe can combine natural and pseudo gradients before one optimizer advance. This differs from our frozen strict alternating pure-gradient steps. It motivates studying joint-gradient updates if the local accumulated-state controls support it. It does not show a local improvement or reproduce the released model.
scope: Read-only source review during the already frozen accumulated-state diagnostic. No active-plan changes, training, code execution from the repository or external datasets. Different NAG optimizer, precision, context1536, model size and sample-size weighting remain important gaps.

supplement.finding: The supplement confirms detached preceding-copy anchors. Its margin variant can over-penalize repetition and has worse reported generation quality; MSE is also weaker. This argues against an ungrounded stronger penalty or alternative-loss sweep.
supplement.limitation: Previous review lacked this supplement; it is now retrieved. No new figure-coordinate estimates or exhaustive supplementary-control claim. Published table outcomes are not local results.
